illus: An illustration

A mason who worked on building sites in the Gulf came home to a village near Thiruvalla for his mother's funeral. He lived in a single rented room with five other men, and everyone knew he sent most of his wages home. At the funeral lunch the parish priest mentioned quietly that the church needed a few thousand rupees to repair a leaking roof over the old people's pew before the monsoon was in full spate. The next morning the mason came to the sacristy with an envelope; he would not say how much it held. The priest told afterwards that the roof was mended that week, and that when he thanked the man, the mason said only: my mother gave everything she had for us, and I do not know how else to learn to do it. The priest said that he had not heard a better sermon on the churches of Macedonia.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this First Friday we thank you for your Heart that gave everything. Teach us to give ourselves first to you, and make our works a sign of the Father's love. Amen.
share: Their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity (2 Corinthians 8:2). Where have I met joy in poverty?
They gave themselves first to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5). What would it mean for me to give myself first, before my gifts?
Believe the works (John 10:38). Which works of mine might lead someone toward the Father?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a heart like yours.
interc: For the Church, that she may give herself first to the Lord and so be generous to the poor.
For the poor and for those who suffer affliction, that they may find help from the generous.
For all who give beyond their means for the sake of others, that God may repay them with joy.
For those who find it hard to believe, that they may see in our works the love of the Father.
For our families, that we may learn to give with a glad heart on this First Friday.
pm.close: Father, you have shown us your good works in your Son. Give us the joy of those who give themselves first to you, and let our lives lead others to believe. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord appoints seventy-two others and sends them ahead of him in pairs to every town where he intends to go.
He tells them to pray for laborers, to bring peace to every house, to heal the sick and to say that the kingdom of God has come near.
St Paul says that the weapons of the messengers of Christ are not human; they have divine power, and authority is given for building up.
2027-07-05.action: Greet your own house with a blessing of peace when you enter it today, and pray for laborers for the harvest.
2027-07-05.question: Where is the Lord sending me ahead of him, and with whom?
term: Shliho (ശ്ലീഹാ)

From the Syriac word for “one who is sent”. The Panchangam calls the Seventy-two “heralds” (അറിയിപ്പുകാർ), those who announce; in Syriac usage the word shliho is used for the Twelve and for Paul, but the idea is the same for all who are sent by Christ with the message.

family.explain: Jesus once sent seventy-two of his friends to go ahead of him to the towns where he was going to visit. He sent them in pairs, so that no one would walk alone. They carried nothing but the good news. When they came to a house, the first thing they said was: “Peace to this house!” They stayed, ate what was given, and helped the sick. Then they told everyone: the kingdom of God is near. These friends of Jesus are called heralds, because they announced that he was coming. We can be heralds too, whenever we bring peace into a house.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters and missionaries, and for ourselves, that we may bring peace wherever we go.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we greet with a word of peace this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Pathanamthitta there was a custom, started by an old catechism teacher, that on the Monday after the first heavy rain two parishioners, always a pair, one grown and one young, walked from house to house along the parish road with a single question: has your roof held? They collected nothing and sold nothing. At each door they said a short prayer of peace on the house, and if the roof had leaked, they noted it and sent a word to the parish council. After some years people no longer called these the roof visits; they called them the peace visits. A family that had stopped coming to church because of a quarrel told the visitors that they had been moved by being asked such a small question by two people who had walked in the rain, and they came back the next Sunday.

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you send us ahead of you to every house and every town. Teach us to pray for laborers, to carry peace, and to say with joy that your kingdom has come near. Amen.
share: The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few (Luke 10:2). For which laborers do I pray, and do I ever answer the call myself?
Whatever house you enter, first say, Peace to this house (Luke 10:5). What would it change if I began every visit and every arrival with a blessing?
The weapons of our warfare are not merely human, but they have divine power (2 Corinthians 10:4). Which weapons do I trust, and which does the Lord ask me to use?
pm.resp: Lord, send laborers into your harvest.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a herald of the kingdom of God in every town and village.
For priests, sisters, catechists and missionaries sent far from home, that the Lord may protect them.
For our parish, that we may carry peace into every house and care for the sick and the lonely.
For all who have been refused a welcome, that they may not lose heart.
For those who have not yet heard the Gospel, that the Lord may send them heralds.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son and you send us in his name. Give us the peace of your kingdom to carry to every house, and keep us lambs who trust in you in the midst of the wolves. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

kidsaint: Mar Addai sent to Edessa

An old story told by Eusebius says that King Abgar of Edessa was very ill and had heard about Jesus and his healings. After the Lord had gone up to heaven, one of the seventy disciples, Thaddaeus, was sent to the city. He prayed for the sick, spoke about Jesus and was welcomed. In the Syriac Churches he is remembered as Mar Addai. Lesson: when the Lord sends us, we only need to go with peace and a kind heart, and he will do the rest.

quick: The Epistle says: remember your leaders, imitate their faith, and know that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
We have an altar from which we are fed; we go out to Jesus outside the camp, looking for the city that is to come; we offer praise and share what we have.
The Gospel asks us to be the faithful and wise servant whom the master finds at work when he comes.
2027-07-06.action: Pray today, by name, for three people who handed on the faith to you, and for one person who has hurt you.
2027-07-06.question: If the Lord came this evening, what would he find me doing?

family.explain: Today the Church remembers Joseph Ramban, a monk-priest, and St Maria Goretti, a brave young girl. The letter tells us to remember the people who taught us about God and to follow their faith. People change, they grow old and they go to God, but Jesus never changes: he is the same yesterday, today and for ever. Jesus also tells us to be good servants who are found doing their work when he comes. Maria was only eleven, but she said no to what was wrong and she forgave someone who hurt her, and God found her ready.
family.intention: We pray for those who taught us the faith, for those who have died, and for children who are in danger or who are hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught you to pray? Let us say thank you to God for them.”

illus: An illustration

In a church near Changanassery the family of an old priest kept his ormma every year on the same day. The younger grandchildren, who had never known him, asked what he had been like. His niece did not describe his sermons. She said that when the first monsoon rains came he would walk the parish roads with a big black umbrella, stopping at every house where someone was ill, and that he was never once seen to hurry. One of the boys asked what he had said to the sick. She answered that mostly he sat with them, and sometimes he said the Lord's Prayer, and then he went home. At the end of the lunch the boy said that he wanted to be like the umbrella man. His niece told the family later that she had never been so moved by a remark; she believed that was exactly how a memory should work.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the same yesterday, today and for ever, we thank you for those who spoke your word to us. Help us to remember them at your altar, to imitate their faith, and to be found faithful when you come. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you (Hebrews 13:7). Who comes to my mind, and what do I want to imitate in them?
Let us then go to him outside the camp (Hebrews 13:13). What comfort am I asked to leave for the sake of the Lord?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What is the work he has given me in my household?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful and wise.
interc: For the Church, that she may remember her leaders with gratitude and imitate their faith.
For monks, nuns, priests and bishops, living and dead, and in a special way for Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban.
For children and young people, that they may have the courage to say no to what is wrong and to forgive.
For those who have been hurt by others, that God may give them healing and a heart ready to forgive.
For all of us, that when the master comes he may find us at work.
pm.close: Father, you gave us leaders who spoke your word, and you gave us a saint who forgave to the end. Keep us faithful, so that your Son may find us watching when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul feels a divine jealousy for the Corinthians: he has betrothed them to one husband, Christ, and fears that another Jesus may lead them astray.
Jesus says that whoever walks in daylight does not stumble; Lazarus has fallen asleep and Jesus goes to awaken him.
Thomas the Twin says: “Let us also go, that we may die with him”, a brave friend, whom we remembered on Saturday.
2027-07-07.action: Choose one fear that keeps you from following the Lord this week and say, “Let us also go.”
2027-07-07.question: Where is the Lord going that I am afraid to follow?

family.explain: When Jesus said that he wanted to go back to Judea, the disciples were afraid, because some people there wanted to hurt him. Jesus told them that whoever walks in the daylight does not trip. Then one friend spoke up: Thomas, who was called the Twin. He said that they should go too and be with Jesus, even if it was hard. He was brave. Last Saturday we remembered St Thomas, who, our tradition says, came all the way to India. The Lord was going to a sad house to awaken his friend Lazarus, who had fallen asleep in death.
family.intention: We pray for families who are sad because someone has died, and that we may be brave friends of Jesus like Thomas.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to follow Jesus? Let us say together: Lord, we will go with you.”

illus: An illustration

One monsoon night a landslide closed the road above Munnar, and a message came to a young catechism teacher that an old man in a lonely hamlet was dying and wanted the priest. The road was dangerous and the rain was heavy. The teacher's friends hesitated. She said, “Let us go, we can walk the last part,” and two of them agreed. They walked for two hours with a torch and one umbrella, found the old man still alive and prayed beside him until the priest arrived at dawn by another route. Afterwards she said she had not felt brave at all; she had only felt that she could not let him die with no one beside him. When the others asked what had made her say it, she remembered the line from the Gospel about Thomas, which she had read that week.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, you walk before us in the day. Give us a pure and simple devotion to you, and the courage to say with Thomas, “Let us also go.” Amen.
share: I am afraid that your thoughts will be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ (2 Corinthians 11:3). What could lead my devotion away from simplicity?
Those who walk during the day do not stumble (John 11:9). When has walking with the Lord kept me from falling?
Let us also go (John 11:16). Whose side am I asked to stand beside, even when I am afraid?
pm.resp: Lord, we will go with you.
interc: For the Church, the bride of Christ, that she may remain faithful and pure in her devotion to him.
For all who are tempted by another gospel, that they may return to the Jesus of the Apostles.
For the sick and the dying, and for those who grieve, that they may feel the nearness of the Lord.
For the Church in India, that she may have the courage of Mar Thoma Shleeha.
For each of us, that we may follow the Lord to wherever he is going.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you have shown us the way, the light of the day, and in your Apostle Thomas the courage to follow him. Keep us faithful and bring us, with all who sleep in him, to the day that has no evening. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul asks Philemon to welcome Onesimus as he would welcome Paul himself, and to charge any debt to Paul's account.
Paul trusts Philemon to do more than he asks, and asks for a guest room and the prayers of the household.
The disciples forget bread; Jesus asks them to remember the loaves and baskets, and warns against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
2027-07-08.action: Welcome one person warmly today, as if Christ himself were the guest, and quietly forgive or take on one small debt.
2027-07-08.question: Have I forgotten what the Lord has already done for me?

family.explain: St Paul wrote a short letter to his friend Philemon about a man named Onesimus. Onesimus had been a slave in Philemon's house and had gone away, but he had met Paul and become a friend of Jesus. Paul asked Philemon to welcome him back as a brother, and said that if Onesimus owed anything, Paul would pay it. In the Gospel the friends of Jesus are worried because they have forgotten to bring bread. Jesus reminds them how he fed five thousand with five loaves and four thousand with seven loaves. He does not want us to worry; he wants us to remember how kind God has been to us.
family.intention: We pray for families who are worried about money or food, and for those who have to forgive someone.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we welcome as a guest this week? What is one good thing God did for us recently?”

illus: An illustration

A grocer in a small town near Pala kept a ledger for credit sales, the kadam book. A widow who bought rice and lamp oil on credit fell behind through a long illness, and the grocer, who was not an unkind man, had begun to speak sharply about it. The parish priest, who heard of it, said nothing to the widow. On the day his own small pension was paid he went to the shop, asked to see the page, and told the grocer to put the amount on his own account. When the widow came to thank him, he waved his hand and said that he had learnt the trick from a very short letter of St Paul. The grocer, who read the letter that night, said later that it was the first time he had understood why the parish kept a guest room in the presbytery.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you welcomed us and took our debts onto yourself. Teach us to welcome one another, to remember all your gifts and to beware of the yeast that spoils. Amen.
share: Welcome him as you would welcome me (Philemon 17). Whom do I find it hardest to welcome?
Charge that to my account (Philemon 18). What have I been asked to carry for someone, and what has Christ carried for me?
Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand? (Matthew 16:9). Which gifts of God should I recall when I worry?
pm.resp: Lord, make us remember and make us welcome.
interc: For the Church, that she may welcome the stranger, the poor and the returning with the welcome of Christ.
For those who are enslaved or trafficked and for all who work in unjust conditions, that they may be released and be treated as brothers and sisters.
For the families who are worried about their daily bread, that they may remember God's generosity and find help.
For those who must forgive a debt or a wrong, that they may do so from the heart.
For our parish and our families, that the yeast of pride and hypocrisy may be removed, and the yeast of the kingdom may work in us.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you took our debt upon yourself and welcomed us as your own. Teach us to welcome and to forgive, to remember your gifts, and to be leavened by your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul says that God has shown mercy to all, and he breaks into praise: “O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God!”
From him and through him and to him are all things: this is the Church's doxology, prayed at every Holy Qurbono.
Jesus, hungry, finds a fig tree with leaves but no fruit: God looks for fruit in us, not only for show.
2027-07-09.action: Say a short prayer of thanks today before you eat: from you and through you and to you are all things.
2027-07-09.question: If Jesus came to me hungry today, what would he find on my branches?

family.explain: St Paul looked at everything God has done and could only say: how deep is God's wisdom! Everything we have, our food, the rain, our home, our family, comes from God, goes through God's hands, and returns to God in thanks. In the Gospel, Jesus was hungry and went to a fig tree that had many leaves but no figs. Jesus wants more than leaves from us; he wants the fruits of kindness, prayer and sharing.
family.intention: We thank God for the rain and for our daily food, and we pray for those who have little.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one fruit of kindness we can bring to Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

At a parish feast in a village near Thiruvalla the church was decorated with hundreds of paper flowers and strings of lights. Before the Qurbono the old sacristan stood at the door and looked at it all. Someone asked whether it was not beautiful. He said: it is beautiful, and the lights are for the eyes, but the Qurbono is for the hunger. He said the Lord came to the fig tree hungry, and what he looks for in a feast is not the lights but whether the people come hungry and go away fed, and whether the poor man at the gate has been fed too. Then he went in and lit the lamps on the altar one by one, saying that these at least were lit for the Lord.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, from you and through you and to you are all things. Make us glad in your mercy and fruitful in your service. Amen.
share: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! (Romans 11:33). When have I been left without words before the mystery of God?
God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all (Romans 11:32). What does it mean to me that mercy is meant for everyone?
He found nothing but leaves (Mark 11:13). Where in my life are there leaves but no fruit?
pm.resp: Lord, make us fruitful in your service.
interc: For the Church, that she may offer to God the fruit of prayer, justice and love and not only outward show.
For the Jewish people, whose gifts and calling God has not withdrawn, and for the growth of respect and friendship between Jews and Christians.
For the hungry and the poor in the monsoon months, and for all who feed them.
For those who feel that God's ways are unsearchable in their own suffering, that they may be held in his mercy.
For our parish, that our feasts may feed the hungry and not only please the eye.
pm.close: Father, you shut up all in disobedience so that you might show mercy to all. Teach us to praise you for the depth of your wisdom and to bear the fruit you look for. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul asks whether Israel has stumbled so as to fall, and answers: by no means; the gifts of God are not taken back.
If the root is holy, so are the branches: the Church lives from the root of Israel's faith and must never despise it.
Coming down from the mountain, Jesus heals a father's only son and gives him back to his father.
2027-07-10.action: Pray the Hail Mary today for a family that has a sick child, and say aloud one psalm of Israel.
2027-07-10.question: Where have I stumbled and believed that I had fallen, when the Lord was holding my hand?

family.explain: A father ran to Jesus because his only son was very ill, and the friends of Jesus could not help. Jesus said, “Bring your son here,” and he healed the boy and gave him back to his father. Jesus is never too busy for a child who is hurting, and he loves the parents who bring them. St Paul adds that we are like branches of a tree whose roots go back to Abraham, so we should love the Jewish people, who first received the Bible, and thank God for them.
family.intention: We pray for sick children and their parents, and for doctors and nurses, especially in the monsoon months when fevers spread.
family.ask: Ask: “Who do we know that needs to be brought to Jesus in prayer today?”

illus: An illustration

A father from the hill country near Thodupuzha came to the church every Saturday carrying his grown son, who had been ill from childhood and could not walk. After the Qurbono the priest once asked him, gently, whether he still believed that his boy would be healed. The man thought for a while and said: Father, I do not know how much faith I have. I only know that I keep bringing him. In the Gospel the father brought his son, and Jesus did the rest. So I bring, and I leave the rest to him. The priest said afterwards that he had not heard a better sermon on the Gospel in all his years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you take us by the hand when we stumble, and you give back what seemed lost. Hold us, heal us and make us thankful for the root from which we live. Amen.
share: Have they stumbled so as to fall? By no means! (Romans 11:11). When has a stumble in my life led to something good?
If the root is holy, then the branches also are holy (Romans 11:16). What do I owe to the faith of Israel and to the faith of my own grandparents?
Bring your son here (Luke 9:41). Whom could I bring to Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, hold us by the hand.
interc: For the Jewish people, beloved of God for the sake of their ancestors, and for friendship and understanding between Jews and Christians.
For parents with sick or disabled children, that they may be strengthened and find help.
For doctors, nurses and carers, especially in this season of fevers and floods.
For those who have stumbled in sin or failure, that they may rise and begin again.
For our parish, that we may be a place where all who suffer are brought to the Lord.
pm.close: Father, you hold your people by the hand even when they stumble. Make us grateful for the root that bears us, and bring us all, healed and forgiven, into the fullness of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul gave up his right to be supported at Corinth so that no one could say he preached for money; his boast was love.
Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light: test the spirits and know them by their fruits.
Jesus calls four fishermen, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people,” and at once they leave their nets.
2027-07-12.action: Do one good deed today for which you ask nothing in return, and tell nobody.
2027-07-12.question: What is my net, and am I ready to leave it if Jesus calls?

family.explain: Four fishermen were mending their nets when Jesus walked by and said, “Follow me.” They left their nets and boats at once and went with him to learn how to help people come close to God. Jesus also calls us, in our family, in school and in work. St Paul teaches us to serve gladly without asking for anything. He also tells us to be wise and ask: does this teaching agree with what the Church teaches?
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and their families, especially in the monsoon when the sea is rough, and for those who are called to serve the Church.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small thing we can leave behind to follow Jesus more closely this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a fishing village near Vizhinjam a young man became a priest. His mother, who had mended nets all her life, could not read well and did not understand the long ceremony. At the end of his first Qurbono, she walked up to the altar with a small piece of old net folded in her hands. She laid it by the chalice and said quietly: I mended nets for my sons all my life. Today I give a net back to the Lord. The people who saw her said later that the sermon had come at the end, and it had been the shortest and the best of the day.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called fishermen to follow you and promised to make them fishers of people. Call us also, and make us ready to leave what holds us. Amen.
share: Immediately they left their nets and followed him (Matthew 4:20). What do I find hardest to leave for Jesus?
I did not burden anyone (2 Corinthians 11:9). How can I serve without asking for something in return?
Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:14). How do I test what I hear about God?
pm.resp: Lord, make us ready to follow you.
interc: For the Church and her pastors, that they may serve without seeking their own gain and be faithful to the faith of the Apostles.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life, that many young people may hear Jesus say, “Follow me.”
For fishermen and their families, and for all who work on the sea in this monsoon season.
For those misled by false teaching, that they may find the truth and the peace of Christ.
For our parish, that we may be generous in giving and quick to follow.
pm.close: Father, you call us by name through your Son. Give us the courage of the first disciples, the generosity of Paul and the wisdom to know your voice, that we may follow you always. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul says: we do not live to ourselves; whether we live or die, we are the Lord's; so we must not judge one another.
Jesus sees the crowds like sheep without a shepherd, and asks us to pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers.
Mar Sheelas (St Silas) carried the Church's peace from Jerusalem to Antioch and sang hymns with Paul in prison.
2027-07-13.action: Pray for a priest or catechist by name today, and for new vocations.
2027-07-13.question: Am I living to myself, or to the Lord?

family.explain: Jesus saw many people who were tired and lost, like sheep without a shepherd, and his heart was full of compassion. He asked his friends to pray that God would send more helpers to bring his love to everyone. Today we remember St Silas, who was one of those helpers. He carried an important letter from Jerusalem to the new Christians and sang praise to God even in prison. We are all God's helpers, because we belong to the Lord.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, sisters and catechists, and for our bishop Antony Mar Silvanos on his name day.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us be a helper of Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

One April the summer rains came early in Kuttanad, when the paddy stood golden and ready for the sickle. The farmers had too few hands, and the grain was beginning to lie down in the water. The parish priest of a village there read the Gospel of the harvest at the Sunday Qurbono, and then simply asked the young men to come with their sickles on Monday. Nearly forty came, some who had not been in the church for months, and they cut for three days in the mud until the last field was in. The old priest said afterwards that nobody had made a speech and the Gospel had been preached all the same. A farmer added that the Lord of the harvest had sent his laborers through the church door.

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, we belong to you in life and in death. Send out laborers into your harvest, and make us ready to be among them. Amen.
share: We do not live to ourselves, and we do not die to ourselves (Romans 14:7). How would my days change if I lived each one as the Lord's?
Why do you pass judgment on your brother or sister? (Romans 14:10). Whom do I judge too quickly?
The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few (Matthew 9:37). What harvest is waiting in my family and parish?
pm.resp: Lord of the harvest, send out laborers.
interc: For the Church and her bishops, especially our own bishop Antony Mar Silvanos on his name day, that they may be faithful brothers and servants of unity.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life from our parish and our country.
For catechists, teachers and all who carry the Gospel to others, that they may be strengthened.
For those in prison and in hardship, that they may, like Paul and Silas, sing the praise of God.
For our families, that we may live not for ourselves but for the Lord.
pm.close: Father, you gave us your Son as Lord of the living and the dead. Make us yours in all that we are, give your Church shepherds and laborers after your own heart, and gather us all into your harvest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Mar (മാർ)

A Syriac title meaning “my lord”, placed before the names of saints, Fathers and bishops, as in Mar Sheelas (St Silas). For women saints the title is Morth (മൊർത്ത്). A bishop takes a new name at ordination, and the feast of the saint whose name he bears is kept as his name day.
kidsaint: Singing in prison

Paul and Silas were put in prison, with their feet fastened in the stocks. It was midnight and it was dark, and they could have been very sad. But they sang hymns to God, and the other prisoners listened. Suddenly there was an earthquake and the doors opened! The jailer was frightened, but Paul and Silas did not run away. The jailer asked how he could be saved, and he and his whole family were baptized that night. Lesson: even when it is dark, we can sing to God, and our singing may help someone else find Jesus.

quick: St Paul says: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth; we are God's field and God's building.
Tomorrow the Church remembers Archbishop Mar Ivanios, who planted in poverty what has grown through God's gift.
Two blind men cry, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!” and Jesus opens their eyes according to their faith.
2027-07-14.action: Thank, today, one person who planted or watered your faith; and say, “Lord, have mercy on us,” three times.
2027-07-14.question: Do I plant and water in the Lord's field, or do I only look for the harvest?

family.explain: A farmer plants the seed and waters it, but he cannot make it grow; only God does that. St Paul says we are all workers in God's field. Some plant, some water, and God gives the growth. In the Gospel two blind men cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us!” and Jesus opened their eyes because they believed. When we ask Jesus for help with a believing heart, he hears us.
family.intention: We thank God for those who taught us to pray, and we pray for the Church founded by Archbishop Mar Ivanios, whose memory we keep tomorrow.
family.ask: Ask: “Who planted the faith in us? Let us name them and thank God tonight.”

illus: An illustration

An old man in a village near Kottarakkara was seen one rainy morning planting a coconut sapling in his compound. A neighbour smiled and said that he would never taste a nut from that tree: it would not bear for seven years, and he was past eighty. The old man went on with his work. He said: I have eaten from my grandfather's trees all my life, and I never once thanked him to his face. Somebody must plant for those who come after. This is the only way I know to say thank you. Years later his grandsons, sitting under the same tree on the day of the first harvest, told the story to their own children.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, only foundation of your Church, from you comes all growth. Make us faithful in planting and in watering, and open our eyes to see you. Amen.
share: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth (1 Corinthians 3:6). Who planted or watered my faith?
You are God's field, God's building (1 Corinthians 3:9). What part of the field has been given to me?
According to your faith let it be done to you (Matthew 9:29). What do I ask of Jesus with an open hand?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, God's field and God's building, that she may grow in unity on the one foundation, Jesus Christ.
For the Syro-Malankara Church on the eve of the commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios, and for the unity of all Christians.
For those who cannot see, in body or in heart, that the Lord may open their eyes.
For farmers planting in this monsoon, and for all who work for a harvest they may not see.
For our parish, that each of us may do our own part and give the glory to God.
pm.close: Father, you give the growth to all that is planted in your name. Bless the labor of those who plant and water in your Church, open our eyes to see your hand in all things, and bring us all to your harvest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul says that God sent his Son, born of a woman, so that we might receive adoption as children; the woman is Mary, the Mother of God.
A woman blesses the womb that bore Jesus; Jesus says that those who hear the word of God and obey it are blessed, and Mary is the first of them.
Mount Carmel, where Elijah saw the little cloud, gave her this name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel, sign of belonging to Jesus.
2027-07-16.action: Pray a decade of the Rosary today, or three Hail Marys, and choose one word of the Gospel to keep this week.
2027-07-16.question: What word of God have I heard and not yet kept?

family.explain: A woman in the crowd said how happy Jesus' mother must be. Jesus said that those who hear God's word and do it are also happy. Mary heard God's word and always did it: “Let it be with me according to your word.” Today we remember her under the name Our Lady of Mount Carmel. Carmel is a mountain by the sea where the prophet Elijah prayed for rain and saw a tiny cloud that grew into a great shower. Some people wear a small brown cloth, called the scapular, to remember that they belong to Mary and want to follow her.
family.intention: We pray for our mothers and grandmothers and for all who carry the faith in our homes, and we give thanks for the rain.
family.ask: Ask: “What word of God can our family keep together this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill parish near Thiruvalla a grandmother had worn the same brown scapular from her wedding day to her eightieth year. Her grandson, a college student, asked her one evening, half teasing, whether she really thought a piece of cloth could save her. She laughed and took out her Gospel, the pages worn thin at one place. She said: this cloth does not save me; Jesus saves me. But when I put it on each morning I remember whose child I am, and Mary's only advice was in the Gospel at Cana: do whatever he tells you. So each morning I read one verse, and I try to do it by evening. The grandson said later that he had never heard the scapular explained so well, and that he started to read the Gospel that week.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, born of a woman for our sake, give us the faith of your Mother: to hear your word and to keep it. Through her prayers make us children of the Father. Amen.
share: Born of a woman, born under the law (Galatians 4:4). What does it mean to me that the Son of God was truly born of Mary?
Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it (Luke 11:28). Which word of God have I heard and not kept?
A little cloud no bigger than a person's hand is rising out of the sea (1 Kings 18:44). Where have I seen small beginnings of grace grow?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may hear the word of God and keep it, as Mary did.
For the Carmelite family in Kerala and throughout the world, and for all who wear the scapular, that it may be a sign of true discipleship.
For mothers and grandmothers who pass on the faith in our homes.
For rain in due season and for farmers and families in the heaviest weeks of the monsoon.
For our parish, that we may be children who say Abba, Father, and disciples who obey.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, born of a woman, to make us your children. Through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, Our Lady of Mount Carmel, give us faith that hears and obedience that keeps your word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Yoldath Aloho (യോൽദത്ത് ആലോഹോ)

The Syriac title of Mary, meaning “she who gave birth to God”, the equivalent of the Greek Theotokos, which the Council of Ephesus (431) used to confess that Jesus Christ is truly God and truly man, and that Mary is therefore truly his Mother. In the Syro-Malankara Church Mary is often honoured in the liturgy under this title.
kidsaint: The little cloud over the sea

The prophet Elijah went up Mount Carmel and prayed for rain because there had been no rain for three years, and everything was dry. He sent his servant to look at the sea. The servant looked and said, “There is nothing.” Elijah told him to look again, seven times! At the seventh time the servant said, “There is a little cloud, no bigger than a hand!” Soon the whole sky was dark, and the rain came down. People later said that the little cloud is like Mary, a small, humble girl from Nazareth, who brought us Jesus, who is like rain for the whole world. Lesson: small beginnings can bring a great blessing, and Mary teaches us to say yes to God.

quick: Paul thanks God, who in Christ leads us in triumph and spreads through us the fragrance of the knowledge of Christ.
In the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus reads Isaiah: the Spirit of the Lord is upon him to bring good news to the poor.
The Panchangam remembers St Alexius of Rome, the Anointed One's way of poverty, and prays for two bishops, Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios.
2027-07-17.action: Do one hidden kindness today for someone poor or lonely, and tell no one.
2027-07-17.question: What do people carry away from me: worry, or the fragrance of Christ?

family.explain: When incense or a sweet flower is near us, we smell it even without being told. St Paul says that people who stay close to Jesus smell like Jesus: kind, gentle and glad. The Holy Spirit was given to Jesus so that he could bring good news to the poor, and he gives us the same Spirit so that we can share his kindness. The Church today remembers St Alexius, who in an old story left a rich home to live among the poor.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, and for families who are poor.
family.ask: Ask: “How can I be the fragrance of Jesus at home today?”

illus: An illustration

In the rains of Karkidakam, a grandmother in a Kottayam house lit a little sambrani on a bit of charcoal in an old coconut shell each evening. The smoke drifted through every room, past the beds and the prayer corner, and her grandchildren said they could tell which house was theirs by the smell on their school bags. One evening a visiting cousin laughed and asked why she bothered, since the damp always came back by morning. She answered that the damp came back, yes, but so did she, and a house is not made clean in one evening. Years later, the cousin said that her own children, when they smelled sambrani on a wet evening, said at once, “This is Ammachi.” The grandmother was never preaching, but the whole house said where she had been and who she belonged to.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, anointed by the Spirit to bring good news to the poor, let us be your fragrance in our homes and parish. Amen.
share: Thanks be to God, who spreads through us the fragrance that comes from knowing him (2 Corinthians 2:14). What do people smell on me?
We are persons sent from God and standing in his presence (2 Corinthians 2:17). Do I speak from his presence or to please people?
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor (Luke 4:18). Who is the poor person God puts in my way?
pm.resp: Lord, let us be your fragrance.
interc: For Most Rev. Thomas Mar Koorilos, on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination, and for Most Rev. Yoohanon Mar Alexios on his name day, that they may serve with joy.
For our bishops, priests and deacons, that they may be sincere ministers of the word of God.
For the poor, the homeless and the lonely, that they may meet the good news in our kindness.
For families in this rainy season, for the sick and for those with damp, crowded homes.
For all who have left comfort for the sake of the gospel, that they may be sustained.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Anointed (Christ, ക്രിസ്തു)

The word Christ is the Greek translation of the Hebrew Mashiach, which means one who has been anointed with oil. Kings, priests and prophets of Israel were anointed. Jesus is the Anointed One in a unique way, because he is anointed by the Holy Spirit himself.
kidsaint: The man under the stairs

Long ago, so the story goes, a young man of Rome named Alexius was very rich. But he wanted to love God more than he loved gold. So he gave up his comfortable life and lived among poor people. After many years he came back to his father's house, but nobody knew him, so he lived quietly under the stairs and was kind to everyone. Lesson: Jesus became poor so that we might become rich, and those who follow him can learn to love people more than things. (This is an old story, and we cannot be sure about its details.)

quick: Paul warns that the mystery of lawlessness is at work, but the Lord Jesus will destroy it with the breath of his mouth; the lost are those who refused to love the truth.
The Pharisees ask for a sign from heaven to test Jesus; he sighs, refuses, and crosses to the other side.
The Panchangam remembers Morth Makrina, sister of Basil and Gregory of Nyssa, whose hidden holy life taught her whole family.
2027-07-19.action: Do not ask God for a sign today. Do the thing you already know is right, quietly.
2027-07-19.question: Do I believe because I love the truth, or because I keep asking for more proof?

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus to show them a special sign, but they were not really listening. Jesus felt sad, and he went away. God has already given us many signs of his love: the Gospel, the Holy Qurbono, the beauty of the world, and good people. Today we remember Morth Makrina, who did nothing loud or showy. She prayed, taught her brothers, and shared with the poor, and her whole family learned about Jesus from her.
family.intention: We pray for those who have doubts about their faith, and for the grace of a quiet and honest heart.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one quiet good thing I can do today so that someone sees Jesus in it?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineering student from a village near Pala came home for the holidays full of questions. At the dinner table he told his grandmother that he would believe in God when he was shown some clear proof. She did not argue. That evening, as always, she lit the lamp in the prayer corner and sat down to say her prayers with the rosary, while the monsoon rain beat on the roof. The next morning, during the heavy rain, she crossed the muddy lane with a covered dish and a warm shawl for a neighbour who was ill and alone, as she had done every day for years. The student walked behind her with an umbrella. On the way back he said, without any smile, that he had a new question: what was it that made her do this every day? She said she had never needed a sign, because she had been given a Saviour. He thought about her answer for a long time afterwards.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave us the sign of Jonah, your death and resurrection. Give us a heart that loves the truth and does not need to test you. Amen.
share: The mystery of lawlessness is already at work (2 Thessalonians 2:7). Where do I see deception around me?
They refused to love the truth and so be saved (2 Thessalonians 2:10). Is there a truth I am avoiding?
Why does this generation ask for a sign? (Mark 8:12). What signs has the Lord already given me?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a heart that loves the truth.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the apostolic faith and not be led astray by false signs.
For those who struggle with doubt, that they may find a patient friend and the light of the Gospel.
For families, that like Macrina's home they may be schools of prayer and charity.
For monks, nuns and all who live a hidden life of prayer.
For the poor and the sick in this rainy season, that they may be sheltered and cared for.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Morth (മൊർത്ത്)
A Syriac title of honour, meaning lady, given to holy women of the Syriac tradition, as Mar (lord) is given to holy men. Morth Makrina is St Macrina the Younger.
kidsaint: The big sister who taught everyone

Macrina was the oldest in a big family. She loved Jesus very much, and she taught her little brothers to pray and to read the Psalms. One of them, Basil, became a great bishop, and another, Gregory, wrote many books. When Macrina grew up, she started a quiet home where people prayed and shared what they had with the poor. She never did anything showy, but everyone who knew her learned to love God. Lesson: you do not need a big sign to show Jesus; a quiet and kind life is a sign too.

quick: Coming down from the mountain, the disciples ask why Elijah must come first; Jesus answers that Elijah has come, in John the Baptist.
Elijah stood alone on Mount Carmel, prayed for rain, and was fed with bread on his journey to Horeb.
Paul says that festivals and sabbaths are a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
2027-07-20.action: Choose one decision this week that settles a divided loyalty, and pray for rain for the farmers.
2027-07-20.question: Where am I still limping between two opinions, and what is the one thing I need to choose?

family.explain: Elijah was a prophet who loved God very much. When there was no rain for a long time, he prayed, and a tiny cloud, as small as a hand, rose from the sea. Soon there was a big rain! When Elijah was tired and sad, an angel gave him bread and water and said: Get up and eat. God also feeds us with the Holy Qurbono. And on the mountain, when Jesus shone, Elijah was there with Moses, but then the disciples saw only Jesus, because Jesus is the one we follow.
family.intention: We pray for farmers and for all who wait for rain, and for those who feel tired or sad.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small thing I can pray for with all my heart this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill village in Idukki, the monsoon came late one year and the paddy seedlings in the terraces turned yellow. After the Sunday Qurbana the vicar asked everyone to pray for rain. An old widow who lived at the edge of the village, whose own small field had been dry for three weeks, went home and opened the west window of her kitchen. Every evening, at the hour of the Angelus, she stood there and said, quietly, that she was only watching for the small cloud. Her neighbours teased her gently. On the ninth evening a grey bank came over the ridge, and by midnight the whole village could hear rain on the tin roofs. The next morning she did not say that she had brought the rain. She said that she had learned to look in the right direction, and to go on looking. The farmers of that hill still say, when the sky is slow to open: Let us go and watch for the small cloud.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you spoke with Elijah on the mountain and fed him on the way. Hear our prayer for the rain and for all our needs, and let us follow only you. Amen.
share: How long will you go limping with two different opinions? (1 Kings 18:21). Where am I divided?
Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you (1 Kings 19:7). What feeds me for the journey?
These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:17). What am I still holding on to that is only a shadow?
pm.resp: Lord, we listen to you.
interc: For the Church, that like Elijah she may stand firmly for the living God.
For farmers and all who depend on the rain, for good harvests and safe homes in this monsoon.
For those who are tired, discouraged or alone, that the Lord may send them bread for the way.
For parents and children, that their hearts may be turned to one another.
For the dying, that they may be fed with the bread of life for the last journey.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Nibiya (നിബിയാ)

The Syriac word for prophet, from the same root as the Hebrew navi. The Syriac calendar remembers the prophets of the Old Covenant by this title: Elijah Nibiya is the prophet Elijah, Daniel Nibiya is the prophet Daniel.
kidsaint: The prophet and the little cloud

Elijah was a prophet who loved God, and he prayed that rain would stop and that it would start again. Ravens brought him bread, and a poor widow shared the last of her flour with him; God made her flour and oil last until the rain came. After a long dry time, Elijah told his servant to look at the sea. Seven times he looked. At last he saw a tiny cloud, as small as a hand, and soon the sky turned black and the rain poured down! Lesson: pray and keep on praying; a tiny cloud can become a great rain.

quick: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, the smallest of seeds, which becomes a tree; and like yeast hidden in three measures of flour.
Daniel blesses the God who reveals deep and hidden things, and sees a stone, cut out without human hands, become a mountain that fills the earth.
Paul says that we who are strong should put up with the failings of the weak, as Christ did, and that the scriptures give steadfastness, encouragement and hope.
2027-07-21.action: Do one small good thing today without telling anyone, and pray three times, however briefly.
2027-07-21.question: What small thing in my life do I think is too little for God to use?

family.explain: A mustard seed is so tiny that you can hardly see it, but it grows into a tall plant where birds can rest. Yeast is hidden in the dough, and after a while the whole dough rises. Jesus says God's kingdom is like that: it starts small and quiet, and then it grows. Daniel was a young man who prayed three times a day, even far from home, and God showed him wonderful things. We can start small too: a little prayer, a little kindness.
family.intention: We pray for small things that need to grow: our prayer, our kindness, our family peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one tiny kindness I can do today that might grow?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in a village near Changanassery began, one year, to sow a row of marigold seeds at the edge of the road near the bus stop, because the place was grey and bare. She had no budget and no permission. Some boys laughed at the little seedlings in the monsoon mud. Three years later the whole stretch of road was yellow and orange each August, the shopkeepers were weeding it, the children of the school brought watering cans, and a stranger from the next village, stepping off the bus, said that the place seemed like a village that someone loved. When people thanked the teacher, she said she had only sown a small packet of seeds, and that the rest had been the rain and the neighbours. She always kept a small packet in her handbag, just in case she passed another bare corner.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the seed and the yeast of God's kingdom. Teach us to trust small beginnings and to pray at every hour. Amen.
share: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed (Matthew 13:31). What small beginning has God given me?
He reveals deep and hidden things (Daniel 2:22). What do I ask God to make clear?
Each of us must please our neighbor for the good purpose of building up the neighbor (Romans 15:2). Whose weakness can I bear this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make your kingdom grow in us.
interc: For the Church, that she may grow like the mustard seed and give shelter to all peoples.
For those who work in small and hidden ways for the good of others, that they may not lose heart.
For those who live in exile or far from home, as Daniel did, that they may keep faith.
For unity in our families and our parishes, that we may glorify God with one voice.
For farmers in this monsoon, for good seed and good harvests.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Parable (ഉപമ)

A short story from ordinary life that Jesus uses to reveal the kingdom of God. It invites the hearer to decide: those who listen with an open heart understand, and those who do not listen hear only a story. The word comes from a Greek word meaning to place beside, to compare.
kidsaint: The young man and the lions

Daniel was a young man who lived far from home, in the land of Babylon, where the king did not worship the true God. Daniel prayed three times every day, with his window open toward Jerusalem. Some men did not like this, and they made the king throw Daniel into a pit of lions! But God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths, and Daniel was safe. Lesson: if we trust God and pray every day, he is with us, even when we are far from home or others do not like what we do.

quick: Mary Magdalene came to the tomb while it was still dark, and stayed weeping outside it after the disciples went home.
The risen Jesus called her by name, Mary, and she answered, Rabbouni; he sent her to his brothers.
Paul says that anyone in Christ is a new creation, and that God has entrusted us with the ministry of reconciliation.
2027-07-22.action: Stay a little longer in prayer today, and tell one person simply what the Lord has done for you.
2027-07-22.question: When I cannot find the Lord, do I go home, or do I stay and keep looking?

family.explain: Mary Magdalene loved Jesus very much. Early in the morning, while it was still dark, she went to the tomb and found it empty. The other friends of Jesus went home, but Mary stayed and cried. Then Jesus called her by name: Mary! At once she knew him. Jesus told her: Go and tell my brothers. And she ran to say, I have seen the Lord! Jesus calls each one of us by name, too, and he sends us to tell others about his love.
family.intention: We pray for those who are sad or who miss someone they love, and for the courage to tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How does Jesus call my name? What is one joyful thing I can tell someone about him?”

illus: An illustration

After the death of her teenage son, a woman in a parish near Kollam began to go to the church garden before dawn every day. She sat on the stone bench under the jackfruit tree and wept quietly, as the first rain of the day fell on the leaves. Weeks went by, and she spoke to no one. One morning the old sacristan, coming to ring the bell for the early prayer, passed her and said her name softly, as he had said it for thirty years: Leelamma. She looked up for the first time in many weeks, and said later that it was as if someone had opened a window. She had not known, she said, that she was still known. She began to speak again, first to the sacristan, then to the priest, and, in time, to other mothers who had lost children. People say she became a ministry of consolation in the parish, and she always said that it began with a single name spoken in the dark.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you called Mary Magdalene by name. Call us too, and send us to tell others that we have seen the Lord. Amen.
share: Mary stood weeping outside the tomb (John 20:11). When have I stayed with the Lord in sadness?
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” (John 20:16). How have I heard the Lord call my name?
Go to my brothers and say to them (John 20:17). To whom does the Lord send me this week?
pm.resp: Lord, you have risen indeed.
interc: For the Church, that, like Mary Magdalene, she may announce the resurrection with joy.
For women and men who suffer, that they may be consoled by the Risen Lord.
For those who weep for the dead, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
For reconciliation in families and communities, that we may be ambassadors for Christ.
For those who have fallen away, that the Lord may call them back as his brothers and sisters.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Rabbouni (റബ്ബൂനി)

An Aramaic word meaning my teacher, my master, a more affectionate form of Rabbi. Mary Magdalene uses it when she recognises the risen Lord, and John tells us that it means Teacher. It shows the warmth of a disciple who has found her Lord again.
kidsaint: The first to say, I have seen the Lord

Mary Magdalene was a friend of Jesus. When Jesus died, she was so sad. Very early on Sunday morning she went to the tomb and cried. Then someone called her name: Mary! It was Jesus! He was alive. He told her: Go and tell my friends. And she ran and said: I have seen the Lord! Lesson: Jesus knows our names, and when we meet him, we want to tell everyone the good news.

quick: Jesus tells his disciples not to be led astray or alarmed, and that the one who endures to the end will be saved.
Ezekiel, a priest among the exiles by the river Chebar, was made a sentinel and promised a new heart and a river of life.
Paul gives thanks that the Father has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son.
2027-07-23.action: Pray for a heart of flesh today, and do one generous act for a neighbour.
2027-07-23.question: When I hear alarming news, do I become afraid, or do I become watchful and loving?

family.explain: Jesus tells us that there will be hard times, but we must not be afraid. He wants us to keep loving, even when others stop. The prophet Ezekiel lived far from home, by a river in Babylon, and God spoke to him there. God promised his people a new heart, a soft heart of flesh instead of a hard heart of stone. God gives us such a heart when we pray and when we forgive. And like a good watchman, we can tell others, kindly, about God's love.
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid because of bad news, and for the courage to keep loving.
family.ask: Ask: “What can I do to keep my heart soft and loving today?”

illus: An illustration

During the great floods in Kerala, a retired schoolteacher in a village near Chengannur watched the water climb up the steps of the parish hall, where the church had opened its doors. She had never held a position in the parish. That night, with the rain still falling on the roof, she sat in the corner of the hall and began to write out names on pages of her old notebook: those who had come, who had medicine to take, who had a baby, who was alone. By dawn she had a list, and a small group of young people who had come to help were using it to share out the dry clothes and the rice porridge. When the water went down, a young man asked her how she had known what to do. She said she had only been afraid, like everyone else, and that she had decided to keep awake and to write down names, because a person who is named is not forgotten. The notebook is still kept in the parish hall.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you taught us to keep watch and to endure. Give us a new heart, and keep our love from growing cold. Amen.
share: Beware that no one leads you astray (Matthew 24:4). What voices are leading me astray?
The love of many will grow cold (Matthew 24:12). How can I keep my love warm?
He has rescued us from the power of darkness (Colossians 1:13). For what do I thank the Father today?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a new heart.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep watch and proclaim the good news to all nations.
For those who live in fear because of wars, floods, sickness or loss, that they may find peace in Christ.
For those far from home, in exile or in migration, that the Lord may speak to them and keep them.
For those whose hearts have grown hard, that the Lord may give them a heart of flesh.
For the dying and the dead, that the river of life may reach them.
pm.close: Lord, hear our prayer.

term: Sentinel (കാവൽക്കാരൻ)

A watchman placed on the wall of a city to see the danger coming and to cry out in warning. The prophet Ezekiel is called a sentinel for the house of Israel; the Church also speaks of pastors and of all believers as watchmen who are to keep awake for the coming of the Lord.
kidsaint: The watchman by the river

Ezekiel was a prophet who lived by a river in Babylon, far away from his home in Jerusalem. God spoke to him there and showed him wonderful things. God said that Ezekiel was like a watchman on a high wall, who calls out when he sees danger, so that people may be safe. God also promised: I will give you a new heart, a soft heart, not a hard one. Lesson: God is with us even far from home, and he can make our hearts soft and kind.

quick: St Paul says that when we turn to the Lord the veil is removed, and with unveiled faces we are changed into his image.
St Sharbel, a Maronite monk of Lebanon, lived twenty-three years as a hermit in prayer and silence and loved the Holy Qurbono above all.
Jesus says that no one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.
2027-07-24.action: Spend two minutes in silence before the cross today, with the phone out of reach.
2027-07-24.question: What do I look at most in a day, and what is it making me like?

family.explain: Jesus asks us to follow him all the way. A farmer who is ploughing a straight line must keep his eyes ahead, not behind. Today we remember St Sharbel, who lived on a mountain in Lebanon, praying and working in silence, so that his heart looked only at Jesus. We cannot all live on a mountain, but we can all look at Jesus every day, in our prayers, at church and in the people around us.
family.intention: We pray for monks, nuns and all who live a quiet life of prayer for the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I can do today that keeps my eyes on Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer in Kottayam told his parish priest that he could not pray: his mind jumped from one thing to another and the ten minutes felt like an hour. The priest gave him a simple task. Every morning, with the phone left in another room, he was to sit before the picture of the Sacred Heart in his house and do nothing but look. For weeks it was boring. Then one evening his mother, passing the door, stopped and said, “You sat just like your grandfather used to when he came back from Qurbono.” He had not noticed that he had started to carry himself the way the old man did. Looking had begun to change him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the glory of the Father. Remove the veil from our hearts, and through the prayers of St Sharbel teach us to turn to you each day. Amen.
share: When one turns to the Lord, the veil is removed (2 Corinthians 3:16). What veil lies over my heart today?
We are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another (2 Corinthians 3:18). Where have I seen the Lord change me or someone I know?
No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God (Luke 9:62). What am I tempted to look back at?
pm.resp: Lord, turn our hearts to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may turn to the Lord with unveiled face and be changed into his image.
For monks, nuns and hermits of every Church, that their prayer in silence may be a blessing to the whole world.
For the Maronite Church and all the Eastern Churches that share our Syriac heritage, in communion with the Church of Rome.
For young people who are being called, that they may hear the voice of the Lord and follow him without looking back.
For the sick and the lonely, that they may know that the Lord has made his home with them.
pm.close: Father, you drew your servant Sharbel to a life hidden in silence, prayer and the Holy Qurbono. Turn our hearts to your Son, that we may be changed into his image, and keep us faithful in following him to the end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Hermit (താപസൻ)

A hermit is a Christian who, with the approval of the Church, lives alone in silence, prayer and penance for the praise of God and the salvation of the world. The Church recognises this way of life (Catechism 920); in the Syriac tradition it has an old and honoured place, from the monks of the Syrian desert to the hermits of the mountains of Lebanon.
kidsaint: Sharbel and the cave

When Sharbel was a boy named Youssef, he looked after the family's cattle on the mountain. While the animals grazed, he would go into a little cave nearby and pray. The other children played, and he prayed; he was not unkind or proud, he simply loved to talk to God. When he grew up, he became a monk and then a hermit, and the whole of his life was a long prayer. Lesson: you can talk to Jesus anywhere, even while you mind the cows.

quick: Paul says that godly grief leads to repentance and salvation, but worldly grief leads to death.
Jesus is not afraid of Herod; he goes on his way to Jerusalem and teaches that the Father's work comes first.
Jesus longs to gather the children of Jerusalem as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but they were not willing.
2027-07-26.action: Say a prayer of sorrow for one fault today, and then go and put it right.
2027-07-26.question: When I have failed, do I run away from God or towards him?

family.explain: Have you ever seen a mother hen when it rains? She spreads her wings wide and all her chicks run under them and stay warm and dry. Jesus says that is how much he wants to take care of us. When we do something wrong, he does not want us to hide from him. He wants us to run to him and say sorry, and he will gather us close.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has hurt someone, that they may have the courage to say sorry.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anything I need to say sorry for tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A boy in Thrissur hit a cricket ball through a neighbour's window. For three days he hid in the house, angry with himself, picking at his food. On the fourth evening his grandmother sat beside him and said, “Your sorrow has been eating you. Let it walk you to the neighbour's door instead.” He took his pocket money and went. The neighbour, who had already guessed, laughed, gave him tea and refused the money, though the boy insisted on coming the next Saturday to sweep the yard. Years later he said it was the lightest he had ever felt in his life. The first kind of sorrow had kept him in the house; the second took him out the door.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you long to gather us as a hen gathers her brood. Give us the sorrow that leads to life, and make us willing to come to you. Amen.
share: Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation (2 Corinthians 7:10). When have I felt that kind of sorrow, and what came of it?
I rejoice, because I have complete confidence in you (2 Corinthians 7:16). How does it feel to be trusted, and whom can I trust more?
How often have I desired to gather your children together, and you were not willing (Luke 13:34). Where am I unwilling today?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us under your wings.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be a mother who gathers all her children.
For those who are ashamed of what they have done, that they may find the courage to return to the Lord.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be gentle and faithful ministers of God's mercy.
For the city of Jerusalem and all who live there, Jews, Christians and Muslims, that it may know the things that make for peace.
For families who have lost a child or a parent, that they may find shelter under God's wings.
pm.close: Father, you long to gather all your children as a hen gathers her brood. Give us the sorrow that leads to life, make us willing to be gathered, and let us enter your house, blessing the one who comes in your name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul says that we walk by faith, not by sight, and that our aim is to please the Lord.
All of us must appear before the judgment seat of Christ, who loved us and gave himself for us.
In the parable the gardener asks the owner for one more year for the barren fig tree, and promises to dig around it and feed it.
2027-07-27.action: Take one small step of faith today, even though you cannot see the whole road.
2027-07-27.question: If the owner of the vineyard came to my life today, what fruit would he find?

family.explain: A man planted a fig tree and waited for fruit, but the tree gave none for three years. He wanted to cut it down, but the gardener said, “Please give it one more year. I will dig around it and give it food.” Jesus is like that gardener. He is patient with us and gives us time, and he helps us to grow good fruit: love, kindness and patience.
family.intention: We pray that we may use the time God gives us to grow in love.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit can I grow this week: kindness, patience or sharing?”

illus: An illustration

An old woman in a village near Kottarakkara had a mango tree behind her house that had flowered every year and never given a mango. Her son wanted to cut it for firewood. She said, “Give it one more year.” That year she dug around its roots, put ash and cow dung at the foot, watered it through the summer, and talked to it as she walked past. In the monsoon the following year it hung with mangoes. Asked how she had known, she answered, “I did not know. I only knew that I had not yet done everything for it.” The people who heard her told it afterwards as a parable about God.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, patient Gardener, give us time and grace to bear fruit. Teach us to walk by faith and to make it our aim to please you. Amen.
share: We walk by faith, not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7). When has trust carried me through when I could not see the way?
Whether we are at home or away, we make it our aim to please him (2 Corinthians 5:9). What would it mean to make this my aim this week?
Let it alone for one more year (Luke 13:8). Where has the Lord been patient with me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bear good fruit.
interc: For the Church, that she may bear the fruit of love in every land and in every season.
For farmers and gardeners in this season of rain, that the fields may be fruitful and the harvest blessed.
For all who feel they have wasted their lives, that they may hear the Gardener asking for one more year.
For the dying, that they may be at home with the Lord in peace.
For ourselves, that we may make it our aim to please the Lord in all things.
pm.close: Father, you are patient and you do not want anyone to perish. Give us a year, a day, an hour in which to bear fruit; dig around our hardness and feed us with your grace, that we may walk by faith and please you in all things. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul says that Christ lives in him and that he lives by faith in the Son of God who loved him and gave himself for him.
Jesus says that a grain of wheat must fall into the earth and die to bear much fruit, and that his servant will be where he is.
Morth Alphonsa, a Clarist sister of Bharananganam, offered a life of illness in love and was made a saint in 2008.
2027-07-28.action: Offer one small pain or disappointment today for someone by name, and keep smiling.
2027-07-28.question: Who or what stands at the centre of my life?

family.explain: When a farmer sows rice seed in the wet field, the seed seems to disappear into the mud. But after some days little green shoots come up, and later there is a whole field of rice! Jesus says that he is like that seed. He died and rose again, and so many people have life through him. St Alphonsa was like that seed too. She was often sick, but she gave all her pain to Jesus with a smile, and now people all over the world come to pray with her.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sick and for those who take care of them.
family.ask: Ask: “What small pain can I give to Jesus today and say, ‘This is for you’?”

illus: An illustration

A woman near Pala nursed her husband for months after a stroke had left him bedridden. She told her parish priest that she could no longer pray long prayers: she had no strength left, and no quiet. He answered, “Every time you turn him in bed, you are a grain of wheat falling into the earth.” On the feast of St Alphonsa she went to Bharananganam in the rain, and a neighbour asked what she had asked of the saint. “Nothing,” she said. “I only told her that I understand her now.” She went home lighter, and the nurse who came to the house the next week remarked that the old man's room had a new calm.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, grain of wheat that died and rose, through the prayers of Morth Alphonsa teach us to give our pain and our lives to you with love. Amen.
share: It is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me (Galatians 2:20). Where do I see Christ living in someone I know?
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain (John 12:24). What am I holding on to that I should let fall?
Whoever serves me must follow me (John 12:26). Whom can I serve this week?
pm.resp: Lord, give us hearts that serve you in love.
interc: For the Church in Kerala and in all India, that the example of St Alphonsa may lead many to give their lives to Christ.
For the sick, that they may unite their pain to the Passion of the Lord and feel his nearness.
For nurses, doctors, caregivers and all who sit beside the suffering, that they may be strengthened.
For the pilgrims who come to Bharananganam, that they may find peace and healing of heart.
For all of us, that we may live by faith in the Son of God who loved us and gave himself for us.
pm.close: Father, you gave your servant Alphonsa a hidden life of prayer and a great love in suffering. Through her prayers help us to live by faith in your Son, who loved us and gave himself for us, and to bear much fruit for your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Morth (മൊർത്ത്)

In the Syriac tradition a male saint is called Mar, “my lord”, and a female saint Morth, “my lady”; the Panchangam therefore writes Morth Alphonsa, Morth Makrina and Morth Yulithi. It is a title of honour, like the word “Saint”.
kidsaint: Annakutty and the smile

Alphonsa was called Annakutty when she was a little girl. Her mother had died when she was a baby, and her relatives took care of her. She loved to pray, and when she grew up she became a sister in a convent at Bharananganam. She was often sick and had much pain, but the sisters who took care of her said that she never complained. She gave her pain to Jesus and she smiled. Today many children and grown-ups go to pray at her tomb. Lesson: when something hurts, you can give it to Jesus and keep smiling.

quick: Hebrews says: do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Martha welcomed Jesus into her home, and Mary sat at his feet and listened; Jesus said that Mary had chosen the better part.
Jesus loved Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany, and he raised Lazarus from the dead.
2027-07-29.action: Invite someone to your home this week, or call someone who is alone, and give them your full attention.
2027-07-29.question: When the Lord comes to my house, am I busy for him or with him?

family.explain: Martha, Mary and Lazarus were great friends of Jesus. They lived in a village called Bethany, and Jesus loved to visit their home. Martha cooked and worked hard, and Mary sat down beside Jesus to listen to him. Jesus loved them both. He wanted Martha to know that listening to him is the most important thing of all. When we welcome visitors and when we pray, we do what Martha and Mary did.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who has no home or no one to visit them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we welcome someone to our house this week?”

illus: An illustration

At a parish feast near Changanassery two women, sisters-in-law, kept the same roles for years. Annamma cooked for three hundred people and never sat in church for the sermon; Mariamma sat in the first pew every day and never entered the kitchen. Each privately believed the other had it wrong. When their old parish priest died, a note was found in his missal: “Annamma, sit in the front pew for once. Mariamma, take the ladle for a day.” They did it, rather stiffly, the next year, and afterwards they shared both. “I did not know what I had been missing,” Annamma said. Mariamma said, “I did not know how heavy the pot was.” The parish still tells it as the story of Bethany.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were welcomed at Bethany. Come into our homes, and teach us to listen to you and to serve you with joy. Amen.
share: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers (Hebrews 13:2). Whom could I welcome this week?
Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things (Luke 10:41). What is distracting me from the Lord?
Mary has chosen the better part (Luke 10:42). Where do I find time to sit at his feet?
pm.resp: Lord, come and stay in our house.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where every stranger is welcomed and every disciple listens to the Word.
For refugees, migrants and all who are far from their homes, that they may find a welcome.
For those who serve in kitchens, hospitals and homes without being seen, that their work may be given to the Lord.
For the communities of the Bethany Ashram and all who join prayer with work, that they may be faithful.
For the dying and the bereaved, that they may hear the Lord say: I am the resurrection and the life.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Son a home at Bethany among the friends he loved. Make us welcoming to him in the stranger, attentive to his word, and faithful in service, that at the last we may be welcomed into your house. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Hospitality (അതിഥിസത്കാരം)

In the Bible welcoming a stranger is a holy duty, not only a courtesy: Abraham welcomed three travellers at Mamre (Genesis 18), Hebrews 13:2 recalls this, and the Lord says that whoever welcomes the least of his brothers and sisters welcomes him (Matthew 25:35, 40). In the Syriac Churches the monasteries have always kept a guest house.
kidsaint: Three friends of Jesus

In a little village called Bethany lived a brother and two sisters: Lazarus, Martha and Mary. Jesus loved to visit their home. When he came, Martha hurried to cook a good meal, and Mary sat down at his feet to listen to every word. One day Lazarus became very sick and died, and everyone cried. Jesus came and cried too, because he loved his friend. Then he called out, “Lazarus, come out!” and Lazarus came out of the tomb alive. Lesson: Jesus is the best friend a family can have. Let us welcome him with a kind heart and listen to him.

quick: Paul says that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, but we are children of light and of the day.
We should not fall asleep as others do, but keep awake and be sober.
Jesus went out at daybreak to a deserted place to pray, and then went on to proclaim the kingdom in other cities, because he was sent.
2027-07-30.action: Get up a little earlier tomorrow and give the first minutes of the day to the Lord.
2027-07-30.question: Am I awake in the Lord, or asleep in routine?

family.explain: Jesus got up very early in the morning, before everyone else, and went to a quiet place to talk to his Father. The people wanted him to stay with them, but he said, “I have to tell other towns about God's kingdom too.” St Paul says that we are children of the light and of the day. That means we should wake up and be ready to do good, just as Jesus did.
family.intention: We pray for people who work at night and early in the morning, for fishermen, bakers, nurses and drivers.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the first thing I will say to God when I wake up tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration
