q: I will not bring upon you any of the diseases that I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you.
Because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross before meals, even in public.

concl: The kingdom belongs to the childlike, and children belong to the kingdom.
Let us become little before God and great in our care for the little ones.
2027-07-25.resolve: Support Sunday school generously, and begin family preparation for the Fifteen Days' Fast next Sunday.

intro: Theme: “And one does not presume to take this honor, but takes it only when called by God, just as Aaron was.”
On Thursday of the sixth week after Pentecost, the memory of Aaron the High Priest: the call of God, the priest who knows weakness, the one High Priest, and the prayer that rises like incense.

sub: Aaron was brought near by the Lord.
No one takes the honour for himself.
The names of the people on his shoulders and heart.
q: Then bring near to you your brother Aaron, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests
You did not choose me but I chose you.
points.apply: Thank God for the call by which one priest was taken from among us, and pray for him by name this week.

sub: The golden calf and the excuses.
The censer between the dead and the living.
Jesus, tested yet without sin.
q: He stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stopped.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: When you see the failing of a priest or of anyone who serves, pray for him before you judge him.

sub: Zechariah inside, the people outside.
The whole assembly was praying.
The prayers of the saints in golden bowls.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
points.apply: At the next Holy Qurbono, when the incense rises, offer to God the names of those you carry in prayer.

concl: God calls his priests from among the people, and he works through them in spite of their weakness, because the one High Priest is Jesus Christ.
The prayer of the people rises with the priest's offering; no one in the church should stay outside.
2027-07-01.resolve: Pray for your priests by name, pray with them at the altar, and let your prayer rise like incense.

intro: Theme: “so that you may know and understand that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.”
On the First Friday, Friday of the sixth week after Pentecost: the joy of Macedonia, the gift of self, and the works that point to the Father.

sub: Affliction, poverty and abundant joy.
Giving according to their means and beyond.
Begging for the privilege of giving.
q: A generous person will be enriched, and one who gives water will get water.
for during a severe ordeal of affliction, their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity on their part.
points.apply: Choose one gift this week that costs you something and give it with joy.

sub: The gift of self before the gift of money.
Christ became poor for our sake.
The pierced Heart of the First Friday.
q: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Before the next gift you give, offer yourself to the Lord in a short prayer.

sub: “I have shown you many good works from the Father.”
The law that calls God's people “gods”.
The Father is in me and I am in the Father.
q: I say, “You are gods, children of the Most High, all of you;
Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; but if you do not, then believe me because of the works themselves.
points.apply: Do one quiet work of love today so that someone may see the Father in it.

concl: Jesus gave himself first, and those who follow him give themselves first and then what they have.
Our works are the way many people first meet the Father who is in Christ.
2027-07-02.resolve: Give yourself first, give with joy, and let your works lead others to the Father.

intro: Theme: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.”
On Monday of the seventh week after Pentecost, the commemoration of the Seventy-two Heralds: sent in pairs, sent with peace, and armed with weapons that are not merely human.

sub: Seventy-two others, ahead of the Lord to every town.
The number points to all the nations.
Two by two, because love needs two.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
As the Father has sent me, so I send you.
points.apply: Ask the Lord where he is sending you ahead of him this week, and find one companion to go with you.

sub: The harvest is plentiful and the laborers are few.
The Lord of the harvest is the one who sends.
The mission begins on our knees.
q: Ask of me, and I will make the nations your heritage, and the ends of the earth your possession.
The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.
points.apply: Pray every day this week for laborers for the harvest, and ask whether the Lord is calling you.

sub: The first word of the herald is a blessing.
Eat what is set before you and care for the sick.
The kingdom of God has come near.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house!’
points.apply: Greet your own house and one neighbour's house this week with a blessing of peace.

points.h: Weapons that are not merely human
sub: Paul called weak in person and strong in letters.
The word as the sword of the Spirit.
Authority for building up, not tearing down.
q: Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, says the Lord of hosts.
Take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
points.apply: Before you answer someone who has hurt you or argued with you this week, say a short prayer for them and speak to build up.

concl: The Lord sends heralds in pairs, with peace and the word, to every town and every house, and the weapons they carry are not merely human.
Every baptized person is a herald: let us pray for laborers and begin by greeting our own house.
2027-07-05.resolve: Pray for laborers, bless every house you enter with peace, and say with joy that the kingdom of God has come near.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

On Tuesday of the seventh week after Pentecost, the memory of Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban with St Maria Goretti: remembering our leaders, the altar, the way outside the camp, and the servant found at work.

sub: Remembering as a school of faith.
Consider the outcome of their lives and imitate their faith.
The Ramban remembered by name.
q: Remember the days of old, consider the years long past; ask your father, and he will inform you; your elders, and they will tell you.
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
points.apply: Pray at the next Holy Qurbono for three people who handed on the faith to you.

sub: Leaders pass; Christ remains.
We have an altar from which we are fed.
We remember the dead at the altar.
q: For I the Lord do not change; therefore you, O children of Jacob, have not perished.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: When you receive the Holy Qurbono this week, thank God that Christ does not change, and bring one departed person to his altar.

sub: Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
Here we have no lasting city.
St Maria Goretti said no and forgave.
q: I am a stranger and an alien residing among you
For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
points.apply: Say no this week to something you know to be wrong, and forgive one person who has hurt you.

points.h: At work when the master arrives
sub: A sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
The faithful and wise slave.
“My master is delayed” is where the fall begins.
q: The faithful will abound with blessings, but one who is in a hurry to be rich will not go unpunished.
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.
points.apply: Do today the work that the Lord has put into your hands, in your household, with praise and with sharing.

concl: The Church remembers her leaders to imitate their faith, and the faith is in the One who does not change.
We are fed at the altar, we go out to him, and we are ready: the master will find us at work.
2027-07-06.resolve: Remember with thanks, forgive from the heart, and be found at work when the Lord comes.

intro: Theme: “Let us also go, that we may die with him.”
On Wednesday of the seventh week after Pentecost: a pure devotion to the one Bridegroom, walking in the daylight of the Lord, and the courage of Thomas the Twin.

sub: Paul's divine jealousy.
The danger of another Jesus.
Keeping our devotion simple and sincere.
q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom’s voice.
points.apply: Test one thing you have heard about Jesus this week against the Gospel and the Creed.

sub: Twelve hours of daylight.
Whoever walks with Jesus does not stumble.
Lazarus has fallen asleep: death is a sleep that the Lord awakens.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.
points.apply: Begin one task you have been postponing out of fear, saying: “Lord, I walk with you.”

sub: Thomas the Twin, brave before he understands.
The Dukrono of Mar Thoma Shleeha, kept on Saturday.
Going to the grieving and the dying.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.
points.apply: Visit a sick or grieving person this week and let your presence say: “Let us go.”

concl: The Church is betrothed to one Bridegroom; let us guard a simple and pure devotion to the Jesus of the Apostles.
Whoever walks with Jesus walks in the daylight and can say with Thomas: Let us also go.
2027-07-07.resolve: Keep your devotion pure, walk in the daylight with the Lord, and say with Thomas: Let us also go.

intro: Theme: “So if you consider me your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.”
On Thursday of the seventh week after Pentecost: Paul and Onesimus, the guest room and the household's prayer, the loaves we must remember, and the yeast to beware of.

points.h: Welcome him as you would welcome me
sub: A slave returning as a beloved brother.
The debt written on Paul's own account.
Christ who paid our debt with his own hand.
q: The alien who resides with you shall be to you as the citizen among you; you shall love the alien as yourself
Welcome one another, therefore, just as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God.
points.apply: Welcome this week one person whom it would be easier to avoid, and forgive or carry one small debt.

sub: The disciples forgot to bring bread.
The five loaves and the seven loaves.
The cure for worry is memory.
q: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits
Do you still not perceive? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you gathered?
points.apply: Each evening this week name three gifts of God from the day.

sub: A little yeast works through the whole batch.
Pride, hypocrisy and the demand for signs.
The warning is for each of us.
q: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses
A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
points.apply: Examine your heart tonight for one small yeast of pride or hypocrisy, and ask the Lord to remove it.

concl: Christ has taken our debt on his own account and welcomed us as brothers and sisters; we are asked to do the same.
The cure for worry is to remember what God has done, and the cure for spoiled yeast is a heart leavened by his kingdom.
2027-07-08.resolve: Welcome, forgive, remember, and let only the good yeast work in you.

intro: Theme: “For from him and through him and to him are all things.”
On Friday of the seventh week after Pentecost: God's mercy for all, the depth of his wisdom, and the fig tree that shows leaves but no fruit.

sub: Paul's sorrow for his own people.
The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
No one has a claim and no one may boast.
q: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
points.apply: Pray today for someone you find hard to love, and ask God to show them the mercy he has shown you.

sub: Paul reasons for three chapters, then adores.
God owes us nothing: all is gift.
The doxology of the Holy Qurbono.
q: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then we will see face to face.
points.apply: Add a sentence of praise to your prayer at meals this week.

sub: The fig tree and the Temple, read together.
Hosea and Jeremiah: Israel as the fig tree God hoped for.
Words without deeds are leaves.
q: When I wanted to gather them, says the Lord, there are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree; even the leaves are withered, and what I gave them has passed away from them.
My Father is glorified by this, that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
points.apply: Name one place in your life where there are only leaves and decide what fruit you will bear there.

concl: God has imprisoned all in disobedience so that he may be merciful to all: we live by mercy, and mercy leaves no room for boasting.
He comes to us hungry, looking for the fruit of prayer, justice and love.
2027-07-09.resolve: Praise God for his mercy, and bear fruit instead of leaves.

intro: Theme: “If the root is holy, then the branches also are holy.”
On Saturday of the seventh week after Pentecost: Paul's question about Israel, the root that bears the Church, and the father who brings his only son down from the mountain to Jesus.

sub: “Have they stumbled so as to fall? By no means!”
God brings good even from a stumble.
The Lord holds us by the hand.
q: though we stumble, we shall not fall headlong, for the Lord holds us by the hand.
So I ask, have they stumbled so as to fall? By no means!
points.apply: If you have fallen in a habit or a promise, go to confession this week and begin again.

sub: First fruits and root.
Wild branches grafted onto the tree.
The psalms and the Alleluia of every Qurbono.
q: and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
points.apply: Thank God for the people of Israel whenever you hear a psalm at the Qurbono, and speak of the Jewish people with respect.

sub: The glory on the mountain, the pain in the valley.
The only child, the disciples who could not.
Jesus raises the boy and gives him back to his father.
q: The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
Immediately the father of the child cried out, “I believe; help my unbelief!”
points.apply: Bring one person in need to Jesus today in a prayer said aloud.

concl: The Lord does not let his people fall: the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable, and he holds us by the hand.
The Church lives from a holy root, and from the altar she is sent to the valleys where the suffering wait.
2027-07-10.resolve: Be grateful for the root, hold on to the Lord's hand, and bring someone in need to him.

intro: Theme: “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
On Monday of the eighth week after Pentecost: the first four disciples leave their nets, Paul serves without being a burden, and we are taught to test the spirits.

sub: Four ordinary fishermen.
“Immediately they left their nets.”
The call and the promise.
q: Then he set out and followed Elijah, and became his servant.
And he said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fish for people.”
points.apply: Name one net you hold on to and place it at the feet of Jesus today.

sub: Paul gives up his right to support at Corinth.
The worker still deserves his living.
“God knows I do!”
q: Whose ox have I taken? Or whose donkey have I taken?
I coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing.
points.apply: Do one service this week for which you ask nothing in return.

sub: False apostles and the angel of light.
The fruit test: humility, love, service.
The faith handed down from the Apostles.
q: The simple believe everything, but the clever consider their steps.
Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God;
points.apply: Before you share or believe a religious message, ask whether it agrees with the Church's faith and whether it bears the fruit of love.

concl: The true call comes in ordinary places and asks us to leave a net; the true servant gives rather than takes.
Not all that shines is of God: we are to know the spirits by their fruits.
2027-07-12.resolve: Leave one net, serve without a price, and test every spirit.

intro: Theme: “We are the Lord's.”
On Tuesday of the eighth week after Pentecost, with Mar Sheelas (St Silas): belonging to the Lord, the compassion of the shepherd, and the laborers for the harvest.

sub: Living and dying to the Lord.
The brother and sister are his too.
No one has the right to despise another.
q: Know that the Lord is God. It is he that made us, and we are his; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; so then, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
points.apply: Say each morning, “I am the Lord's,” and pray for someone you were tempted to judge.

sub: The messenger of peace from Jerusalem to Antioch.
Praying and singing hymns in the prison at Philippi.
Companion of Paul and, as Silvanus, of Peter.
q: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
Through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother, I have written this short letter to encourage you
points.apply: Be a carrier of peace this week: bring a kind word between two people who are not on speaking terms.

points.h: Ask the Lord of the harvest
sub: The crowds like sheep without a shepherd.
The harvest is plentiful, the laborers few.
First pray, then be sent.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.
points.apply: Pray for vocations from your parish, and answer “Here am I” to one small task in the Church.

concl: We belong to the Lord in life and in death, and so does every brother and sister we are tempted to judge.
The Lord of the harvest looks at the crowds with compassion and asks us to pray, and then he sends us, as he sent Mar Sheelas.
2027-07-13.resolve: Live this day as the Lord's, judge no one, and pray for laborers.

intro: Theme: “I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.”

On Wednesday of the eighth week after Pentecost, the eve of the commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios: the planters of our faith, God's field and building, and the two blind men whose eyes are opened.

sub: Paul and Apollos are servants.
The one who plants and the one who waters share a purpose.
Every harvest is God's gift.
q: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
points.apply: Do your part of a task this week faithfully, and hand over the result to God in prayer.

sub: A field tended season after season.
One foundation, Jesus Christ.
Those who planted our faith, and the memory of Mar Ivanios.
q: They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, to display his glory.
For no one can lay any foundation other than the one that has been laid; that foundation is Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Thank one person who planted or watered your faith, and say a prayer for the unity of the Church.

sub: The blind men see who Jesus is.
Faith is an open hand.
Gratitude cannot keep silent.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped;
Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”
points.apply: Pray the cry of the blind men three times a day: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us.

concl: The Church is God's field and God's building; we plant and we water, and God gives the growth, on the one foundation which is Christ.
The cry Have mercy on us opens our eyes to see his hand in all the growth we have received.
2027-07-14.resolve: Plant and water faithfully, thank those who planted before us, and give the glory to God.

intro: Theme: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
On Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Friday of the eighth week after Pentecost: the Son born of a woman, the blessedness of hearing and keeping, and the little cloud over Carmel.

sub: The Son of God took flesh from Mary.
Theotokos and Yoldath Aloho: Mother of God.
Through him we are children and heirs.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
points.apply: Say the Hail Mary slowly today, thinking of the words “the fruit of thy womb, Jesus”.

points.h: Blessed are those who hear and keep
sub: The woman in the crowd and the word “rather”.
Mary's yes, her pondering, her faith.
Augustine and Lumen Gentium 58.
q: All that the Lord has spoken we will do, and we will be obedient.
Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.
points.apply: Choose one word of Sunday's Gospel and keep it all week.

points.h: Carmel: the garden and the little cloud
sub: Elijah's prayer after three years of drought.
The cloud no bigger than a hand.
The Carmelites, the scapular, and Carmel in Kerala.
q: The glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the majesty of Carmel and Sharon.
he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.” Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.”
points.apply: If you wear the scapular, renew what it means; if not, ask Mary to teach you to hear and obey.

concl: Mary is the Mother of God and the first and best of those who hear the word and keep it.
The little cloud over Carmel and the scapular on the shoulder point to the Son, the rain of grace.
2027-07-16.resolve: Hear the word of God, keep it, and take Mary for your Mother.

intro: Theme: “For we are the aroma of Christ to God.”
On Saturday of the eighth week after Pentecost: the fragrance of Christ, the Anointed One sent to the poor, and St Alexius of Rome.

sub: The incense of the procession.
Paul is not the victor; Christ is.
A fragrance of life to those who welcome it.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us, a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.
points.apply: Pray for one minute before leaving home that others may meet Christ's kindness in you.

points.h: Sent from God, standing before him
sub: Not peddlers of God's word.
Sincerity from the presence of God.
The pastors remembered today.
q: But the Lord said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a boy’; for you shall go to all to whom I send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.”
points.apply: Speak one honest word this week that you were tempted to soften.

points.h: The Anointed sent to the poor
sub: Nazareth, on the sabbath, as was his custom.
Good news, release, sight, liberty.
Today this scripture is fulfilled.
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed,
how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of kindness today for a person who is poor or lonely.

sub: The old Life of St Alexius.
He who was rich became poor.
The pastors we remember today.
q: Happy are those who consider the poor; the Lord delivers them in the day of trouble.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Pray by name for Thomas Mar Koorilos and Yoohanon Mar Alexios and for your own pastors.

concl: The gospel spreads like fragrance through people who have stood in Christ's presence.
The Anointed One is sent to the poor, and so are those who are his.
2027-07-17.resolve: Carry the fragrance of Christ, speak with sincerity, and bring good news to the poor.

intro: Theme: “Why does this generation ask for a sign?”
On Monday of the ninth week after Pentecost: the mystery of lawlessness, the love of the truth, the sign refused, and Morth Makrina.

points.h: The breath of the Lord's mouth
sub: The mystery of lawlessness is at work.
False signs and wonders deceive.
The Lord Jesus overcomes without an army.
q: with the breath of his lips he shall kill the wicked.
But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
points.apply: When you feel afraid of the evil around you, say the name of Jesus and trust his faithfulness.

sub: The danger is a heart that does not love what is true.
God hides nothing from those who seek.
Truth is a person, Jesus.
q: Lead me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all day long.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Take up one question of faith you have put off and read the Gospel on it.

sub: The Pharisees test him.
The deep sigh of the Lord.
The only sign: the sign of Jonah.
q: do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness, when your ancestors tested me, and put me to the proof, though they had seen my work.
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.
points.apply: Do what you already know is right without asking God for proof first.

sub: Teacher of her brothers.
A home of prayer, psalms and charity.
Her life was the sign.
q: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Do one hidden good deed at home this week, without comment.

concl: The Lord gives himself to those who love the truth, and gives no show to those who only test.
A quiet life of prayer and charity, like Macrina's, is a sign that God is near.
2027-07-19.resolve: Love the truth, stop testing the Lord, and shine quietly in good works.

intro: Theme: “they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.”
On Tuesday of the ninth week after Pentecost, the memory of Elijah the Prophet: Elijah has come, the prayer for rain, the bread for the journey, and the shadow and the substance.

sub: Malachi's promise.
Elijah has come in John the Baptist.
The forerunner shares the Lord's fate.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.
With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children,
points.apply: Ask the Lord to turn the hearts in your own family towards one another.

sub: Alone on Mount Carmel.
How long will you go limping?
A human being like us.
q: How long will you go limping with two different opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.
Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain, and for three years and six months it did not rain on the earth.
points.apply: Pray persistently this week for one good thing you are waiting for.

sub: Despair under the broom tree.
The angel and the bread.
A sound of sheer silence.
q: Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
points.apply: When you are weary, rest and eat, and receive the Holy Qurbono as food for the way.

sub: The prophets point ahead.
The substance belongs to Christ.
Listen to him.
q: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Suddenly when they looked around, they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.
points.apply: Put down one thing you cling to that is only a shadow, and hold fast to Christ.

concl: Elijah teaches us to choose, to pray with persistence and to eat the bread God gives.
All the prophets point ahead; the substance is Christ, the head of the body.
2027-07-20.resolve: Choose the Lord, pray without giving up, eat the bread for the way, and follow Jesus alone.

intro: Theme: “the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed.”
On Wednesday of the ninth week after Pentecost, the memory of Daniel the Prophet: the seed and the yeast, the hidden things revealed, the stone that fills the earth, and steadfast prayer.

sub: The kingdom begins small.
Hidden, like yeast in the flour.
It grows until it shelters all.
q: But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field;
points.apply: Do one small, hidden good deed today and trust God to make it grow.

sub: Daniel's blessing of God.
Light dwells with him.
Parables proclaim what was hidden.
q: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with him.
I will open my mouth to speak in parables; I will proclaim what has been hidden from the foundation of the world.
points.apply: Bring one question to God in prayer this week and wait for light.

sub: The tree of pride was cut down.
The tree of the kingdom grows from the smallest seed.
An everlasting kingship.
q: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed,
For, in fact, the kingdom of God is among you.
points.apply: Look for the signs of the kingdom among you this week, and thank God for them.

sub: Daniel's prayer three times a day.
He bore his people's sins in prayer.
Christ did not please himself.
q: he continued to go to his house, which had windows in its upper room open toward Jerusalem, and to get down on his knees three times a day to pray to his God and praise him,
For whatever was written in former days was written for our instruction, so that by steadfastness and by the encouragement of the scriptures we might have hope.
points.apply: Pray at three set times today, and pray for someone whose failing you must bear.

concl: The kingdom comes through the small and the hidden, and the prophets teach us to be steadfast.
Christ did not please himself; we bear one another and glorify God with one voice.
2027-07-21.resolve: Trust the small seed, pray at the hours, bear one another, and glorify God with one voice.

intro: Theme: “I have seen the Lord.”
On Thursday of the ninth week after Pentecost, St Mary Magdalene: a woman delivered, the one who stayed and wept, called by name, and sent to the brothers.

sub: Magdala and the seven demons.
Faithful at the cross and the burial.
She is not the sinful woman of Luke 7.
q: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?
And the one who was seated on the throne said, “See, I am making all things new.”
points.apply: Thank the Lord for one way in which he has made you new, and speak of it.

sub: While it was still dark.
The disciples went home; she stayed.
The love that seeks is the love that finds.
q: Scarcely had I passed them, when I found him whom my soul loves.
But Mary stood weeping outside the tomb.
points.apply: When prayer is dry, stay ten minutes longer and tell the Lord everything.

sub: Known by being called by name.
Rabbouni.
Do not hold on, but go.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
points.apply: Sit in silence for five minutes and ask the Lord to call you by name.

sub: Sent to the brothers who had fled.
The ministry of reconciliation.
Ambassadors for Christ.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’
points.apply: Tell one person what the risen Lord has done for you, and reconcile with someone who is distant.

concl: The Lord is found by love that stays, and known when he calls us by name.
The first to see the risen Lord was the first sent to announce him, and so are we.
2027-07-22.resolve: Stay and seek, listen for your name, and go and tell: I have seen the Lord.

intro: Theme: “But the one who endures to the end will be saved.”
On Friday of the ninth week after Pentecost, the memory of Ezekiel the Prophet: do not be led astray, the sentinel, the new heart and the river, and the rescue and transfer into the kingdom.

sub: No timetable, but a way to live.
The birth pangs lead to birth.
Love that does not grow cold.
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
By your endurance you will gain your souls.
points.apply: Check and pray before you share alarming news this week.

sub: Ezekiel among the exiles by the river Chebar.
The scroll sweet as honey.
A watchman warns so that people may live.
q: Mortal, I have made you a sentinel for the house of Israel; whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall give them warning from me.
Keep awake therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
points.apply: Speak one gentle word of warning or of care to someone you love.

points.h: A new heart and a river
sub: The heart of stone and the heart of flesh.
Can these bones live?
Everything lives where the river goes.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
As the scripture has said, ‘Out of the believer’s heart shall flow rivers of living water.’
points.apply: Ask the Lord each morning this week for a heart of flesh.

sub: Out of the power of darkness.
Into the kingdom of the beloved Son.
Endurance rests on what Christ has done.
q: and everything will live where the river goes.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
points.apply: Each evening this week give thanks to the Father for rescuing us.

concl: The Lord gives no timetable but a way to live: watchful, loving, enduring.
He has rescued us and given a new heart; the river of life flows from his side.
2027-07-23.resolve: Be watchful and not alarmed, keep your love warm, and endure to the end.

intro: Theme: “With unveiled faces … we are being transformed.”
On Saturday of the ninth week after Pentecost, with St Sharbel: the veil taken away in Christ, the hermit of Annaya, and the plow that does not look back.

sub: Moses' shining face and the veil.
Only in Christ is it set aside.
Turning to the Lord every day.
q: the Israelites would see the face of Moses, that the skin of his face was shining;
For it is the God who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Each morning this week, turn to the Lord for two minutes before you look at anything else.

sub: We become like what we look at.
The mirror of the Gospel and the altar.
From one degree of glory to another.
q: Look to him, and be radiant; so your faces shall never be ashamed.
but be transformed by the renewing of your minds
points.apply: Choose one thing you look at too much and give its time to the Gospel this week.

points.h: St Sharbel, the hermit of Annaya
sub: From Bekaa Kafra to the monastery of St Maron.
Twenty-three years in the hermitage of Sts Peter and Paul.
A Syriac saint who loved the Holy Qurbono.
q: Be still, and know that I am God!
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Give a quiet half hour this week to prayer, without a screen.

points.h: The plow that does not look back
sub: The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
Elisha and the oxen.
Keeping the Lord first in a family and a job.
q: Then he set out and followed Elijah, and became his servant.
forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal
points.apply: Take the first step this week on one thing the Lord has asked you to do and you have postponed.

concl: When we turn to the Lord the veil is removed, and looking at him changes us into his image.
St Sharbel gave twenty-three years of silence to that gaze; every disciple gives the Lord the first place and does not look back.
2027-07-24.resolve: Turn to the Lord every morning, give him a quiet half hour, and keep your hand on the plow.

intro: Theme: “Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation.”
On Monday of the tenth week after Pentecost: two kinds of sorrow, the Lord who does not fear the fox, and the hen who gathers her brood.

sub: Worldly grief turns inward.
Godly grief turns to God.
Peter and Judas.
q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Take one burden you have carried alone to the Sacrament of Reconciliation this week.

points.h: The Lord who sets his face
sub: Warned of Herod, unafraid.
The Father's timetable.
The road to Jerusalem.
q: I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
points.apply: When fear tells you to turn back from something good, pray for the courage of the Lord who set his face.

sub: How often have I desired to gather your children.
You were not willing.
Under his wings you will find refuge.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge;
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it,
points.apply: Each time you feel afraid or ashamed this week, say: Lord, gather me.

concl: Godly grief is simply the moment when we stop being unwilling and run to the Lord who longs to gather us.
He sets his face towards Jerusalem for us, and under his wings we find refuge.
2027-07-26.resolve: Choose godly sorrow, run to the Lord with it, and let him gather you.

intro: Theme: “We walk by faith, not by sight.”
On Tuesday of the tenth week after Pentecost: the small lamp of faith, the aim to please the Lord, and the Gardener who asks for one more year.

sub: A lamp for the next step.
Trust in the Lord whom we do not yet see.
At home in the body, away from the Lord.
q: but the righteous live by their faith.
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
points.apply: Take the first step on one decision you have put off because you cannot see the whole road.

sub: Whether at home or away.
The judgment seat of the Christ who loves us.
Every deed, good or evil, before God.
q: For God will bring every deed into judgment, including every secret thing, whether good or evil.
enter into the joy of your master.
points.apply: At the end of each day this week ask: What did I do today that pleased the Lord?

sub: The owner's patience and the gardener's plea.
Digging and feeding: grace at work.
Now is the acceptable time.
q: In old age they still produce fruit; they are always green and full of sap,
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit to grow this week and practise it daily.

concl: We walk by faith, not by sight, with the single aim of pleasing the Lord who will be our judge and who loves us.
The Gardener asks for one more year and works at our roots; today is that year.
2027-07-27.resolve: Walk by faith, aim to please the Lord, and let the Gardener work on you today.

intro: Theme: “It is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me.”
On Wednesday of the tenth week after Pentecost, with Morth Alphonsa: the new centre of life, the grain of wheat, the Clarist sister of Bharananganam, and the pain that is given in love.

sub: Crucified with Christ.
The Son of God who loved me.
Everything is grace.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
For to me, living is Christ and dying is gain.
points.apply: Start each day this week with the prayer: Lord Jesus, live in me today.

sub: The seed that seems to rot in the wet earth.
The Cross as seed, the Resurrection as harvest.
The disciple goes where Jesus goes.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
Fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
points.apply: Name one thing you clutch at and let it fall into the earth for love of Christ.

sub: From Kudamaloor to the Clarist convent.
Years of illness in prayer and patience.
Canonised on 12 October 2008, the first woman of Indian origin to be a saint.
q: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will ever touch them.
For those who want to save their life will lose it, and those who lose their life for my sake will find it.
points.apply: Visit or ring one sick person this week and give them an hour.

sub: Christ has given suffering a new meaning.
United with the Passion of the Lord.
The saints pray for us.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases;
always carrying in the body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made visible in our bodies.
points.apply: Offer one small pain today for a person you name.

concl: Christ has taken the centre of our life, and the grain that falls into the earth in love bears much fruit.
Morth Alphonsa gave her illness to the Lord with a smile, and her hidden life has fed thousands.
2027-07-28.resolve: Let Christ live in you, give your small pains in love, and serve the sick.

intro: Theme: “Mary has chosen the better part.”
On Thursday of the tenth week after Pentecost, with Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany: the welcome of a home, the one thing needed, and the friends whom Jesus loved.

sub: Do not neglect hospitality to strangers.
Abraham ran out to meet three travellers.
Martha opened the door.
q: He said, “My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant.
for I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me,
points.apply: Invite one person who is alone to your home this week.

sub: Mary at the Lord's feet.
Martha called by name, with love.
Worried and distracted by many things.
q: One thing I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in his temple.
Whatever your task, put yourselves into it, as done for the Lord and not for your masters,
points.apply: Give five minutes each morning this week to listening to the Gospel, before any task.

sub: Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
Martha's confession: the Messiah, the Son of God.
Mary's tears and perfume; Lazarus called out of the tomb.
q: he will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord God will wipe away the tears from all faces,
Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.
points.apply: Say the confession of Martha slowly today: Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God.

sub: Work and prayer belong together.
Bethany Ashram, founded by Mar Ivanios in 1919.
At the Holy Qurbono the Lord serves us himself.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Mary took a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
points.apply: Serve one household task today without grumbling, and pray as you do it.

concl: Martha and Mary are two halves of one discipleship: the welcome that serves and the listening that loves.
Jesus loved the house at Bethany, and he comes to our homes and to his table to serve us himself.
2027-07-29.resolve: Welcome the stranger, sit at the Lord's feet, and serve without grumbling.

intro: Theme: “You are all children of light and children of the day.”
On Friday of the tenth week after Pentecost: the thief in the night, the call to keep awake and sober, and the Lord who rises at daybreak to pray.

sub: We are not of the night or of darkness.
The day of the Lord comes like a thief.
A thief surprises the sleeping, not the watchful.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
For once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light.
points.apply: Each night this week say: Lord, I am a child of your day; keep me awake in you.

sub: Not fear, but alertness in the Lord.
A clear head in a noisy world.
Destined for salvation, awake or asleep.
q: O Lord, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you, and watch.
And what I say to you I say to all: Keep awake.
points.apply: Give the first ten minutes of the morning to prayer, before the phone and the news.

sub: He rises early and prays in a deserted place.
The crowds want to keep him.
He goes on, for he was sent.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
He answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim the message there also; for that is what I came out to do.”
points.apply: Ask the Lord today where you are sent, and go there.

concl: We belong to the day: no thief of the night can surprise those who are awake in the Lord.
The Lord himself rises at daybreak to pray, and then goes where he is sent; we follow him.
2027-07-30.resolve: Keep awake and sober, begin the day in prayer, and go where you are sent.

intro: Theme: “Do everything for the glory of God.”
On Saturday of the tenth week after Pentecost, with St Ignatius of Loyola: the ordinary day given to God, the cost of discipleship, and the soldier who found a greater cause.

points.h: Everything for the glory of God
sub: Eating, drinking, working: nothing is too small.
Seeking the good of many, that they may be saved.
The motto: to the greater glory of God.
q: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
points.apply: Before each meal and each task today say: To the greater glory of God.

sub: The builder and the king.
Hate father and mother: the first place for Christ.
Following him with open eyes.
q: By wisdom a house is built, and by understanding it is established;
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
points.apply: Think of one good work you have begun and ask the Lord for what you need to finish it.

sub: Wounded at Pamplona in 1521.
The lives of Christ and the saints.
The Spiritual Exercises and the Society of Jesus.
q: What shall I return to the Lord for all his bounty to me?
For what will it profit them if they gain the whole world but forfeit their life? Or what will they give in return for their life?
points.apply: Make the examen tonight: five minutes of looking back over the day with thanks.

sub: Carry the cross and follow.
Francis Xavier on the coast of India.
Every state of life is called.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.
points.apply: Choose one good example of a believer you know and imitate it this week.

concl: Paul asks us to do everything for the glory of God, and the Lord asks us to count the cost before we follow him.
St Ignatius gave his whole life to that greater glory, and sent Francis Xavier to the coast of India.
2027-07-31.resolve: Do everything for the glory of God, count the cost, and carry the cross after the Lord.
